transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I suppose I'm here because... things have just been a bit off lately. My father-in-law moved in with us a while back, and, uh, it's been an adjustment. I keep it together on shift—I'm an EMT, so I have to—but at home and with my coursework, I'm just... wound up, I guess. Shorter with people than normal. I haven't even been going out fishing or doing my woodworking... haven't even gone to the extra first-aid workshops I usually like. Just haven't had it in me.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities like fishing or woodworking that you used to enjoy?
Yeah... like I said, I just haven't been doing them. I don't know if I'd call it a loss of pleasure, exactly. I just... haven't really felt like it lately.
Have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, lately?
No, not really. I wouldn't say I'm depressed. Just... tired, mostly.
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating or focusing on tasks, like your coursework or other activities?

I haven't really noticed any big changes there. I mean, my coursework is getting done. I wouldn't say I'm having trouble focusing, just... maybe a bit less motivated to sit down and do it. But I get through it fine.
Can you describe how you feel when you think about doing woodworking or going fishing now, compared to how you felt about them before your father-in-law moved in?

I don't know... it's not really a big feeling one way or the other. Before he moved in, I guess I just did those things when I had some time off. Now... I just don't really think about it much. By the time I have a minute to myself, I'm just... tired. It's not a big deal, I just haven't been doing them.
When you think about doing woodworking or going fishing, do you feel any sense of enjoyment or satisfaction just from thinking about it, or does it feel like there's no point in doing it anymore?
I don't know if there's no point... I just don't really think about it. I don't get any big feeling from thinking about it, I guess. I just don't have the energy right now.

When you think about woodworking or fishing—things you used to do—do you still feel any sense of pleasure or satisfaction just from thinking about them, or does it feel like those things don’t bring you any joy anymore?

I guess... I don't really know. Like I said, I just don't think about them much right now. It's not that I think they wouldn't be fun, I just... I'm too tired to even consider it. I don't really feel much of anything when I think about it.

When you think about the times you used to go fishing or work on your woodworking projects, do you remember feeling pleasure or satisfaction from them, or does it feel like you didn’t get anything out of them even back then?

I mean... yeah, they were fine. I liked them well enough back then. It wasn't... I don't know, it wasn't some huge thing. Just normal stuff to do on a day off. I guess I got something out of it at the time.
When you think about doing something you used to enjoy, like fishing or woodworking, does it feel pointless to even try, or like it wouldn’t be worth the effort?
I don't know about pointless. It's just... a lot of effort. I just don't really want to do it right now.
When you think about doing something you used to enjoy, like fishing or woodworking, does it feel like those things wouldn’t bring you any pleasure anymore, even if you did them?
I don't really know if they would or wouldn't. I just... I haven't tried. Like I said, it's just hard to work up the energy to even think about trying.
When you think about doing something you used to enjoy, like fishing or woodworking, does it feel like those activities wouldn’t bring you any pleasure anymore, even if you tried them?
I... I think I just answered that. Like I said, I really don't know. I haven't tried, so I can't really say if I'd enjoy it or not.
When you think about doing something you used to enjoy, like fishing or woodworking, does it feel like those activities wouldn’t bring you any pleasure anymore, even if you tried them?
Look, Doc... you keep asking me the exact same thing. I really don't know what else to tell you. I haven't tried. I don't know if it would feel good or not. I just don't know.

When you imagine yourself doing something you used to enjoy, like fishing or woodworking, do you feel any pleasure or satisfaction just from picturing it in your mind, or does it feel like it wouldn’t be enjoyable at all?
I just... I can't picture it right now. I don't know what it would feel like.

When you imagine yourself doing something you used to enjoy, like fishing or woodworking, do you feel any pleasure or satisfaction just from picturing it in your mind, or does it feel like it wouldn't be enjoyable at all?
I just... we're going in circles here. I can't picture it. I don't feel anything when I try. I don't know what else to say about it.

When you think about the things you used to enjoy, like fishing or woodworking, does it feel like you’re completely unable to feel any pleasure or happiness from them, even when you imagine doing them?
Look, you're asking the exact same question again. I... I don't have a different answer for you. I just don't know.
In general, do you find that you can still feel pleasure or joy from things you used to like, or does pretty much everything feel less enjoyable lately?
I... I guess pretty much everything feels less enjoyable. I just don't get much out of things right now.
When you participate in something you used to enjoy, like fishing or woodworking, do you find that you can no longer feel the same sense of pleasure or satisfaction, even when you do them?
I haven't really been doing them. So... I don't know.
